decision.summaryForCoordinator: This successor differs from the FX-5 and FX-6 ones in a way you should know: FX-7 v1 was NEVER independently reviewed — no verdict file of any kind exists for it — so nothing in this chain was already verified and the repair was an author-side self-correction rather than a response to a recorded rejection. That made the subject's own claim about its predecessor the first thing to test, and it is exact. It says v1's fx7Intent 'was a 320-of-404 true prefix'; measured against v1's bytes, v1 is 320 characters, live is 404, v1 != live, and live.startswith(v1) is TRUE. So the artifact diagnoses its own predecessor correctly and without overstating — a true prefix is the milder defect shape, and it does not claim the altered-quotation form I found in FX-6 v1. The restoration itself lands: fx7Intent == live at 404 against 404, recovering v9's honesty sentence 'A single differing decision means a clock or an arrival order entered the ordering', and fx7Proves is present and == equal to live where v1 had no such field. The numeric prohibition is the sharp one here and it holds: the complete bare-integer set is 0, 2 and 26; every time unit probed returns zero; and the apparent 'ns', 'us' and 'sec' hits resolve to substring noise inside words like perturbations, status and 'section 7.1'. The only content numbers are 320 and 404, hyphen-joined inside the predecessor role, and both are verified character counts rather than fixture values. Two things are worth your attention. First, the clockStepSize and delayDuration placement is precisely reasoned rather than uniform: clockStepSize sits on the two STEPPED states and not on the frozen one, because a frozen clock has no step to size, and delayDuration sits on the delayed state and not on the reordered one, because reordering has no duration. Applying both to all five would have been the easy error. Second, the whole-object diff surfaced an improvement the intent restoration did not require: v1 cited permission-fx5-input-corpus.v1 at ea47fc7d — the version I REJECTED — annotated 'Awaiting independent review'; v2 drops that entry entirely and cites the accepted v2 at a1f95e81 instead. Re-pointing a citation off a rejected artifact onto its accepted successor is the right repair and nobody asked for it. Every /initialStates path is byte-identical between v1 and v2, so the five perturbations themselves are untouched. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at 5e79e3b4 and 0444 at both samplings, v1 unmoved at 693d8e26 and 0444, six of six cited digests equal live bytes, both sibling standings confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict anywhere in this family, the D-163 join confirms OBL-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with owner none and FX-7 inside its fourteen, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, no control bytes, SATISFIED and QUALIFIED at zero. Chronology rules out staleness — the subject was authored at 07:19:46, after both cited verdicts landed. Seventeen attacks run, seventeen refuted, zero findings. One thing to note rather than fix: the lands array carries a defect-class description rather than a finding id, which is the honest choice given that no FX-7 finding exists, but if you want lands reserved strictly for finding ids then a differently named field would carry the same information unambiguously.
